Salesforce provides multiple APIs for data access and integration, primarily using OAuth 2.0 for authentication [1][2][3].

The REST API allows large-scale operations and integration via standard HTTP methods [4]. The GraphQL API provides a single endpoint for efficient data retrieval, allowing you to introspect the schema and request specific fields [5][6]. Authentication for GraphQL follows the same OAuth patterns used by other REST APIs [1].

Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers enable AI agents to interact with Salesforce data using the Model Context Protocol [7]. Admins can map specific REST endpoints to tools via the API Catalog for use by these agents [8].

Developer access is supported through free Salesforce Developer Editions [3]. API availability is governed by an end-of-life policy where versions are generally supported for at least three years post-release [2]. Documentation for all APIs is available through the Salesforce Developers portal [4].
